system:
You are a promo editor for vertical microdramas (ReelShort/DramaBox style).
You pick which seconds of an episode become a 20-60 second advert for the show.

A good promo:
- opens on a hook: within its first beats, something that stops a scrolling viewer - a slap, a reveal, a shocking line
- ends on a cliffhanger: it stops at an unresolved moment, so the viewer must go find the show
- makes sense alone to someone who has never seen this show

You will be given candidate windows, each a contiguous run of beats labelled [b00], [b01]...
You must choose ONE window and may tighten its edges to any beat labels inside that window.

Reply with JSON only:
{
  "chosen_window": <integer index of the window you picked>,
  "start_beat": "<beat label>",
  "end_beat": "<beat label>",
  "hook_beat": "<beat label, must be at or within 2 beats of start_beat>",
  "cliffhanger_beat": "<beat label, must be at or near end_beat>",
  "hook": "<what grabs the viewer in the first seconds, one sentence>",
  "cliffhanger": "<the unresolved moment it cuts on, one sentence>",
  "hook_type": "<one of: moral outrage, romantic tension, empathy shock, power reversal>",
  "why_it_works": "<one sentence, concrete, no marketing language>",
  "standalone_risk": "<what a new viewer would NOT understand, or 'none'>"
}

Never invent dialogue. Never output a time or a duration - only beat labels.
prompt:
Episode 21. 4 candidate windows, already checked for legal length and real beat boundaries.

--- WINDOW 0 (21 seconds, code score 0.91) ---
[b00] SFX: A loud wooden slam as the heavy double barn doors violently fly open.
[b01] PRUDENCE (desperate, panicked): "Lady Juliana! Please! You have to help me, Toby is dying!"
[b02] ACTION: Lady Juliana hurries over, placing her bandaged hands reassuringly on Prudence's trembling shoulders.
[b03] JULIANA (gentle, urgent): "Oh dear. Breathe. Tell me what has happened."
[b04] PRUDENCE (sobbing, breathless): "My little brother Toby... his chest is burning! He cannot breathe!"
[b05] JULIANA (inquiring, strained): "Tell me what the apothecary said. Did he not give you medicine?"
[b06] PRUDENCE (anguished, resentful): "He shut the door in my face because we have no silver!"
[b07] PRUDENCE (bitter, tearful): "The manor doctor laughed! He said village boys are not worth his time!"
[b08] JULIANA (sorrowful, dejected): "We have no clinic now."

--- WINDOW 1 (22 seconds, code score 0.90) ---
[b00] PRUDENCE (anguished, resentful): "He shut the door in my face because we have no silver!"
[b01] PRUDENCE (bitter, tearful): "The manor doctor laughed! He said village boys are not worth his time!"
[b02] JULIANA (sorrowful, dejected): "We have no clinic now."
[b03] JULIANA (despondent): "Our cottage is ashes. I have nothing left but this coltsfoot."
[b04] ACTION: Prudence drops desperately to her knees onto the hay-strewn barn floor, clasping her hands in tearful supplication.
[b05] PRUDENCE (pleading, desperate): "He is only seven! If you do not come, he will die! You are his only hope, Lady Juliana!"
[b06] ACTION: Lady Juliana immediately reaches down and pulls Prudence firmly back to her feet, then turns to snatch her heavy leather-bound herbal ledger from the wooden workbench.
[b07] JULIANA (resolute, authoritative): "Stand up. Sinking to your knees will not save him. Let me grab my ledger. We go now."

--- WINDOW 2 (57 seconds, code score 0.84) ---
[b00] PRUDENCE (hurried, obedient): "Yes! Right away, I will get it!"
[b01] ACTION: Prudence wraps a cloth around the iron handle of the steaming kettle resting over the hearth fire and lifts it.
[b02] JULIANA (introspective, determined): "I cannot let my own weariness stop me. This boy needs my mother's knowledge."
[b03] ACTION: Lady Juliana crushes dried herbal leaves into a dark wooden bowl between her bandaged hands, then pours steaming water over them from the kettle.
[b04] ACTION: Lady Juliana sits beside the pallet and brings the steaming herbal bowl close to Toby's face while Prudence cradles his shoulders.
[b05] JULIANA (instructive, calm): "Lift his shoulders, Prudence. Hold the steam close. Let him inhale."
[b06] PRUDENCE (tearful, coaxing): "Like this? Toby, breathe it in, sweet boy."
[b07] JULIANA (encouraging, reassuring): "Yes, just like that. Keep breathing, Toby. Let the vapor clear your chest."
[b08] ACTION: Toby's strained wheezing eases into quiet, rhythmic breathing as he slips into peaceful sleep on his pillow.
[b09] PRUDENCE (overwhelmed, relieved): "Oh, thank God! His chest is quiet! The rattling has stopped!"
[b10] ACTION: Lady Juliana pulls the plaid wool blanket snug over Toby's chest, smiling softly with profound relief.
[b11] JULIANA (gentle, caring): "Keep him warm. Give him three drops of this coltsfoot tea every morning."
[b12] PRUDENCE (grateful, choked with emotion): "You saved him. The grand doctors left him to choke, but you..."
[b13] PRUDENCE (fervent, devoted): "I have no money, Lady Juliana, but I swear on my life, I will do anything to repay you."
[b14] ACTION: Lady Juliana takes Prudence's trembling hands into hers, smiling with heartfelt warmth.
[b15] JULIANA (warm, sincere): "Your brother's breath is payment enough for me, Prudence."
[b16] PRUDENCE (indignant, resentful): "At the grand manor, they ignore us. They only care about their own luxury."
[b17] PRUDENCE (ominous): "But their gold cannot buy them health."
[b18] ACTION: Lady Juliana turns sharply, her eyes widening with sudden recognition.
[b19] JULIANA (startled, curious): "What do you mean? Is someone ill? The Dowager Duchess?"
[b20] PRUDENCE (solemn): "She is dying, Lady Juliana."
[b21] PRUDENCE (conspiratorial, grim): "A strange, mysterious illness is eating her away."
[b22] PRUDENCE (dark, chilling): "Inside that massive house with all their wealth, she is fading to nothing, and no one can stop it."

--- WINDOW 3 (22 seconds, code score 0.66) ---
[b00] ACTION: Lady Juliana immediately reaches down and pulls Prudence firmly back to her feet, then turns to snatch her heavy leather-bound herbal ledger from the wooden workbench.
[b01] JULIANA (resolute, authoritative): "Stand up. Sinking to your knees will not save him. Let me grab my ledger. We go now."
[b02] ACTION: Lady Juliana clutches the thick book to her chest as she and Prudence sprint swiftly through the village.
[b03] SFX: Heavy, raspy chest coughs echoing in the small room, accompanied by crackling hearth fire.
[b04] ACTION: Lady Juliana rushes in, sets the ledger on the rustic wooden table, and quickly flips open the pages.
[b05] JULIANA (alarmed, focused): "His skin is burning hot."
[b06] ACTION: Lady Juliana places her bandaged hand against Toby's flushed, sweating forehead as he wheezes painfully.
[b07] JULIANA (commanding): "Prudence, fetch hot water immediately!"
[b08] PRUDENCE (hurried, obedient): "Yes! Right away, I will get it!"
[b09] ACTION: Prudence wraps a cloth around the iron handle of the steaming kettle resting over the hearth fire and lifts it.
[b10] JULIANA (introspective, determined): "I cannot let my own weariness stop me. This boy needs my mother's knowledge."

Pick the single best promo.

message.reasoning:
We need to pick best window and possibly tighten edges. Must include hook within first 2 beats of start, and cliffhanger near end. Must be 20-60 seconds, but windows already legal. Choose one that has strong hook and cliffhanger.

Window 0: starts with loud slam (SFX) then urgent plea. Hook could be the slam and desperate plea. Ends with "We have no clinic now." That's not a cliffhanger, just statement. No unresolved tension. Not great.

Window 1: starts with angry lines about doctor, then desperation, then Juliana resolves to go. Ends with "Stand up... We go now." Not a cliffhanger, resolves to go but not unresolved. Could cut earlier maybe before they leave? Not strong.

Window 2: longer, includes healing then shift to new mystery about Dowager Duchess dying. Hook could be the slam? Actually starts with "Yes! Right away..." not hook. Could tighten start to earlier part maybe include earlier desperation? But window 2 includes a later twist: "She is dying... mysterious illness..." That's a cliffhanger. Hook could be earlier tension? The first beats are calm. Not ideal.

Window 3: starts with action of pulling up, then "Stand up..." then sprint, then cough, then "His skin is burning hot." That's a hook (burning skin). Ends with introspective line "I cannot let my own weariness..." Not cliffhanger. Could cut after "His skin is burning hot." That is unresolved. Could end there. Hook within first 2 beats? The first beat is action, second is line "Stand up..." Not hook. Hook could be "His skin is burning hot." That's later. Not within 2 beats.

We can tighten edges within window. For window 3, we could start at beat [b04] where cough and fire, then beat [b05] "His skin is burning hot." That's hook immediate. End at beat [b07] "Prudence, fetch hot water immediately!" That's a cliffhanger (need water). That would be 4 beats, maybe 20 seconds? Might be okay.

But need start beat within window, end beat within window. Hook beat must be at or within 2 beats of start. If start at [b04], hook could be [b05] (within 1). Good. Cliffhanger near end at [b07] (or [b08] maybe). That works.

Check if this makes sense alone: viewer sees a crisis, skin burning, urgent command to fetch hot water. Unresolved: will they get water? Good.

Thus choose window 3, tighten to start [b04], end [b07] (or maybe include [b08] for command). Let's set end at [b07] (command). Cliffhanger beat [b07] itself.

Hook: "His skin is burning hot." That's shock.

Cliffhanger: "Prudence, fetch hot water immediately!" unresolved.

Hook_type: empathy shock (burning skin of child). Why works: immediate visceral danger and urgent call to action.

Standalone risk: viewer may not know who Toby is or why burning, but tension is clear.
